newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand held below the 4.70 level against the dollar on Thursday, despite strong local and offshore dollar demand, as the Reserve Bank moved in to cap the currency's slide above 4.69, dealers said.
Exporter demand for rand and importer demand for dollars made for reasonable turnover but business was less hectic than in the previous two roller-coaster sessions.
"The market was nervous after yesterday -- it's been a lot quieter," said one forex trader.
"But we've seen some fair two-way business with exporters and importers both in, while the SARB (South African Reserve Bank) has been watching the top, coming in above 4.69," he said.
Dealers said the market remained nervous of a test of the 4.70 level in New York trade after the market's bumpy ride this week which saw it retrace sharply on Wednesday from a low of 4.64.

Bonds had a subdued day and yields ended unchanged after trading in a narrow range. Traders reported some institutional demand but said most funds were staying on the sidelines in the face of a choppy currency.
"I think we would have seen far more institutional demand if it wasn't for the rand. The rand in the 4.70 area is scary," said one dealer.

Attention remained focused on the short-end of the market as banks raised three-month buy rates by five basis points. But the money market shortage edged down marginally on Wednesday and economists said any official rate hike appeared unlikely before the end of the month or early December -- if at all.
"I would say there is a very low probability of the Reserve Bank hiking Bank rate at this stage," said Herman van Papendorp of SMK Securities.

Analysts said governor Chris Stals would likely wait for October money supply and bank credit growth figures due at the end of this month, and third quarter current account data due in the next Reserve Bank Quarterly Bulletin due on December 5.
BOE Natwest economist Nick Barnardt said the interest rate position was finely balanced with a 50/50 chance of a hike in Bank rate -- currently 16 percent -- at the end of November or early December.
The rand was last at 4.6870/20 against dollar from 4.6830/80 on Wednesday. Against the crosses, it was at 7.7991/8121 from 7.7373/7502 against sterling and at 0.3213/17 marks against 0.3212/16.
The yield on the R150 benchmark long bond was last at 16.10 percent, unchanged from Wednesday's local close.
Foreigners sold a net 111.66 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying a net 51.08 million rand on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 7.01 billion rand on Wednesday from 3.98 billion rand on Tuesday.
Three-month NCD rates ended at between 16.95 and 17.20 percent from 16.85 and 17.10 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was hiked to 16.30 to 16.75 from 16.25 to 16.45 percent.
The daily money market shortage for Wednesday was 9.677 billion rand on Wednesday from Tuesday's 9.810 billion rand.
